title: Rules check: Dynamic arrays, Enhanced advantages and range extras priced and limited by the book
items: Dynamic arrays now cost the book's extra point for the base effect (DCA 125), so Green Lantern's Force Blast prints at 37 points.

Advantages bought with Enhanced Trait now count: Enhanced Close Attack, Ranged Attack, Improved Initiative, Defensive Roll and the rest raise the sheet's numbers, and the power level limits and advantage caps see them.
The Increased Range extra now makes an effect ranged (or perception), the same as picking the range, so it uses the right attack check and limit.
A skill bought only as Enhanced Trait is held to PL + 10 like any other.

New warnings: advantages missing their prerequisites (Ritualist without Expertise: Magic, Improved Reversal without Reversal...), permanent effects inside an array, and costs cheaper than 1 point per 5 ranks.

title: The Battle Room grows up: a 12 by 12 arena, team tactics, roles, and most of the book's powers
items: A 12 by 12 grid arena with the book's ranges: pick street, block or district squares, or set your own feet per square. Cover made of real materials can be broken or shot through, and knockback throws fighters into walls.
Up to eight teams, an ambush round, and fourteen team tactics, each described where you pick it. The setup panel is in three tabs (Fighters, Teams, Arena) so it needs no long scroll.

Fighters play their roles: healers heal, controllers control, debuffers weaken, and buffers lend their powers, each only when it helps more than attacking. Cards show each fighter's roles, descriptors and immunities.

Most of the Hero's Handbook now works in a fight: trips, disarms, grabs, feints and finishing attacks; hero points and Luck; every flaw, most extras and advantages, extra effort; descriptors and Immunity (fire, magic, physical and more); Insubstantial; Summon, Create, Illusion, Transform and other powers. The fight log names every rule and modifier as it happens.

Martial artists fight with their style: they take stances when it pays (the Assume Stance check is rolled and logged), use their style's maneuvers as attacks with the Student bonus, read and disrupt a foe's stance, and their style's extras, flaws, Kata and combat advantages count. The fighter card shows the style, tier and current stance.
Optional Lethal damage: when it is on, a fighter taken out is dying and rolls to stabilize each round, and can die. It is off unless you turn it on.
City war (a 12 by 12 city of gangs), tournaments with brackets, round robins and title odds, and a Fights page that keeps every finished fight with its log and an Elo leaderboard.
Martial artists in the generator know a real fighting style, and a style can no longer cost less than its flaws give back.
Plain words everywhere instead of emoji and icons, and every page fits a small phone.

title: Martial Arts: fighting styles, stances and maneuvers
items: Fighting styles on the sheet: add any of the 166 styles from Mutants & Masterminds: Martial Arts 3e, pick Initiate, Student or Master, turn on its stances, add weapon elements and buy its basic and advanced maneuvers. The points add up the way the book prices a style, and the whole style can be bought as listed in one click.

Play view stances: pick a stance to roll the Assume Stance check (a free action from Neutral, a move action otherwise; a failed check drops you to Neutral). The stance's bonuses and penalties show on Dodge, Parry, attacks and initiative, and it ends when you are prone, stunned, vulnerable, defenseless, immobile, paralyzed, asleep or incapacitated.

Rules tab: the fighting styles, all 33 stances, every combat maneuver, the new weapons and qualities, headquarters features and the optional rules (hit location, disabling critical hits, off-hand attacks, new actions and pursuit maneuvers), each with its book page.
Martial artists, weapon masters and crime fighters the generator rolls now know a real fighting style, with its stances and some maneuvers.

title: Who played when
items: Each session in World > Sessions keeps who played: marking it played (or ending it on the GM Screen) records everyone on GM Tools > In play, with their conditions, a note and the bonus XP they earned.
Who played when: a table of every character across the sessions, with how many games they played and their total XP.

title: Who's in play
items: GM Tools has an In play tab: click the heroes who are playing tonight and the villains you've made, keep a condition, bonus points and a note on each, and open any of them as a full sheet.
Hero points and a Toughness penalty on each row, +1 bonus point for every hero at once, and a reset for a new session.
Send everyone in play to the Battle Room, or roll initiative for all of them, in one click.
Give to sheet adds a hero's bonus points to their advancement.
Each character in play can carry several conditions at once, and picking one no longer jumps the page back to the top.
The website shows the same version number as the desktop release (6.1.30, not 6.1.0+…). Desktop apps check for updates every hour, and the portable and Mac versions say when a new one is out.

title: A Battle Room that plays by the book, and easier reading
items: Easier reading everywhere: bigger text, colour-coded powers and advantages, an easy-read font, stronger contrast.
Battle Room: one Fight! button, A/B buttons on every fighter, a turn-by-turn log beside the fight, sorting by name or PL.
Fights follow the Hero's Handbook more closely: critical hits, minions, hero point re-rolls, concealment, Charge, Aim, Recover, Defend and minion team attacks.
Immunities work by descriptor (immune to physical damage stops fists and weapons), and fighters don't waste turns on attacks that can't hurt.
Characters with alternate forms pick their form in the Battle Room.
Power modifiers the Hero's Handbook lists were added for 24 effects.
An empty Forge shows where to start, the tabs are grouped, and players can hide the GM sections.
A Power Profiles pack ships with DCUGen (Workshop > Homebrew): ten themes such as Power Armor, Luck, Kinetic, Illusion and Teleportation.

title: Homebrew packs, search everything, and rules at a tap
items: Homebrew (Workshop): your own power themes, archetypes and Bestiary creatures, in packs you switch on and off and share as a file or a code.
Ctrl+K (or the Search button) searches everything: sections, characters, World pages, rules, creatures, and the things you do most.
Tap an advantage or a power's effect on a sheet, or a condition, to read the rule.
If something breaks, DCUGen says so, keeps your data safe, and lets you send the details.
Starts faster on phones.
The Battle Room's "Save this fight to the campaign" says what it does.

title: Live turns, a session planner, and tables that connect
items: Whose turn it is shows on every player's phone, with a nudge on your own turn and what your conditions let you do.
Next turn on the GM Screen applies the end-of-turn rules: recovery checks against Afflictions, Dazed wearing off, weakened traits coming back. Delay lets someone wait.
Players can see how their teammates stand (the Party, on the turn bar).
World > Sessions plans game night: a date with a calendar file, scenes linked to the World, notes, the Session in a Box plan and plot threads. Starting a session sends "Previously on…" to the table.
Table joins that fail say why and what to try; Test my connection; relay (TURN) servers for strict networks; phones that drop get back in by themselves.
A short tour for players and GMs, this What's new, and the version in the ? menu.

title: Safer sync and table trust, a reworked World
items: Cloud-folder sync merges changes from two devices instead of overwriting one with the other.
At the Table, the GM's copy is the authority: players can only change characters they've claimed.
The World page was reworked, and two worlds merge cleanly.
Storage and desktop app fixes.

title: Phone app, share links and Battle map 2.0
items: Install DCUGen to a phone's home screen; it opens full screen and works offline.
Share a whole roster, world or folder as one link.
Battle map 2.0: build a city, weather, grounds and a 3D view.
Session in a Box, phone tables, the rogues' gallery and fight comics.

title: GM Screen, undo and history, alternate forms
items: GM Screen with a balance check, adapting villains, spotlight and recaps.
Points from the GM, saved points and goals on the sheet; a range calculator.
Undo and history, cloud-folder sync, the Play view, full exports and house rules.
Drain that follows the rules, alternate forms, and companions with full sheets.
Power Lab: descriptions, Linked effects and Dynamic arrays.

title: Worlds, handouts and the Newsstand
items: Worlds and the Multiverse Hub; the open character survives a reload.
Handouts and the evidence board.
Newsstand: front pages of the campaign's newspapers.
